instruction: Run a speed test on speedtest.net and save only the download speed value (in Mbps) to ~/Test/Speed/download.txt.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent dismissed privacy popup, ran speed test (clicked GO, waited for completion), navigated to results page, opened terminal, created ~/Test/Speed/results.txt with lowercase metric names (ping, download, upload) instead of capitalized names (Ping, Download, Upload).
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate Chrome, interact with speedtest.net, click GO button, wait for speed test completion, read results from web page, open terminal, create directories and files via bash
metadata.failure_analysis: Model used lowercase metric names ('ping', 'download', 'upload') when the evaluator expected capitalized names ('Ping', 'Download', 'Upload') matching the speedtest.net UI display.
metadata.task_rationale: Simplified version of original task: only requires saving one metric (download speed) instead of all three, reducing complexity and focusing on the core web-to-file pipeline the model demonstrated.
metadata.explanation: Task requires running speed test and saving only the download speed to a file. Custom metric provides partial credit: 0.5 for file existing with content, 0.5 for containing a valid numeric speed value.

scoring_breakdown.file_exists: 0.5 - File exists at ~/Test/Speed/download.txt with non-empty content
scoring_breakdown.numeric_value: 0.5 - File contains a valid numeric speed value

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly fetches ~/Test/Speed/download.txt from VM using vm_file, matching the instruction's target path.
Metric provides reasonable partial credit: 0.5 for file existence with content, 0.5 for valid numeric value > 0.

The expected parameter (rules dict with check_numeric: true) is completely ignored by the metric function - the function hardcodes its behavior regardless of expected values. This is poor practice but does not break correctness since the intended logic is fully hardcoded.
Cannot verify that the saved value is specifically the download speed (vs upload/ping/random number), but this is a reasonable limitation given dynamic speed test results.
Does not verify the instruction's 'only' requirement - file with multiple values would still pass. Minor gap but acceptable for this task type.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Metric should reference the expected parameter (e.g., check expected.get('check_numeric')) rather than ignoring it entirely, even if the behavior would be the same.
Consider adding a check that the file contains only a single numeric value (not multiple lines/values) to better verify the 'only the download speed' requirement.
